mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days during easing cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero return).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment rate below 5.0% signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of instances when UNRATE is below 5.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which accelerates economic expansion and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in 60% or more of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In supply chain disruption regimes, constrained industrial production (INDPRO below 95.0) signals reduced economic output and potential inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO is below 95.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized) indicates a robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in 60% or more of quarters with GDPC1 growth above 2.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero return).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 3.0% triggers expectations of aggressive monetary tightening, which increases equity discount rates and causes negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of instances when CPIAUCSL is above 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero return).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strong payroll growth (PAYEMS above 100k) and declining unemployment (UNRATE below 5.0%) signal a rapidly strengthening labor market, boosting consumer confidence and driving positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS > 100k and UNRATE < 5.0% fails to produce positive 5-day returns in 60% or more of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS above 3.0%) signal reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 3.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 vs. zero return).
